item: 7.13 Pinned commands — a row of chips above the composer sends a pinned command in one click; pinned and unpinned on the / menu's rows; the rest fold into +N when the row is too narrow; chips are dragged to reorder (2026-11-22)
branch: js/65-slash.js: setPins (the __cmdPins seed) / togglePin (the .pi-pin toggle renderSlash draws on every row; sends the whole list as bridge kind cmdPins) / renderPins (a chip only for a pin whose command is in the roster and enabled by cmdKind; label = the description's first line, else /name) / runPinned (no argument: sent alone at once, the draft untouched, queued while a turn runs; takes an argument: '/name ' is written in front of the draft and nothing is sent) / layoutPins (chips that do not fit are [hidden], counted on +N and listed in #pinMenu). Markup: #pins in chat.html, styles in css/60-composer.css and css/70-popups.css. Reordering: mousedown / document mousemove / mouseup in the same file (a drag starts after 5px, the chip is re-inserted before the first visible chip whose midpoint the pointer has not passed, the release commits through reorderPins and the click that follows is swallowed).
provenance: No CLI wire frames beyond the roster: the feature is the panel's own. The roster is fed through the panel's __commands host frame with the shapes the CLI sends — a custom command carries the ' (user)' description suffix markCustom parses (measured 2.1.228, fixture 105's provenance), a built-in carries none; `config` stands for any built-in the panel does not enable (cmdKind 'tui'). The __cmdPins seed and the cmdPins bridge frame are this change's own contract with Kotlin (ChatPanel.kt, SavedCommands.parsePins — unit-tested). USER DESIGN 2026-11-22: two mockups and the picks made in the session — the row ABOVE the card (candidate A of three rendered in the real panel), the command's text as the label, an arrow on a chip that sends and a text cursor on one that only fills the box, the command alone with the draft left as it is, global pins, no shortcuts. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN 2026-11-22 against the 242 sandbox still serving the previous build (2506a26, no #pins element and no pin functions): 8 passed, 22 failed: every assert that reads the feature failed and the GUARDs passed — the asserts are written null-safe so a missing element fails an assert instead of throwing and aborting the suite. The first run on the new build then failed ONE assert, step 1's 'the menu stays open': the pin toggle's redraw removes the clicked button, so the document-level click handler saw a target outside every .popup and closed the menu — fixed with stopPropagation in the toggle branch. Fixed build 30/30, whole suite 1320/1320 under JCEF. Step 5b (drag to reorder) was added the same day: negative control on the build without it 30 passed / 5 failed (all of 5b — its trailing click SENT the command), with it 35/35; and a REAL mouse drag (CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent, 25px steps) moved the last of five chips to the front in the sandbox, order saved, nothing sent. The grip glyph on the chip in hand was added after that (two more asserts in 5b: 2 failed without it, 37/37 with it; whole suite 1327/1327), and a real-mouse press-and-move showed the grip displayed and the arrow hidden mid-drag.
